key_insight: Combine dynamic-scene SfM that isolates a moving vehicle from static clutter with a distortion-aware Gaussian splatting renderer to produce high-fidelity 3D vehicle exteriors from drive-through footage despite lens distortion, specular paint, and rotating wheels.
problem_solved: Accurate, scalable reconstruction of vehicle exteriors captured in cluttered dealership drive-throughs where the subject moves, backgrounds are static but busy, lenses are wide-angle, and surfaces are highly specular or partially non-rigid (wheel rotation).
method: Dynamic-scene SfM pipeline that segments and tracks the moving vehicle separately from the static background to recover robust geometry and camera poses.
Distortion-aware camera modeling and calibration to correct wide-angle lens effects before reconstruction.
Gaussian splatting-based surface representation optimized for specular reflections and per-frame non-rigid effects (e.g., wheel rotation), producing dense, photoreal outputs.
impact: Enables practical, drive-through capture workflows for generating production-quality 3D vehicle assets at scale, improving virtual showrooms, AR experiences, and training data for downstream vision systems. Makes photogrammetric reconstruction robust to motion, clutter, and optical distortions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input drive-through video → dynamic SfM (segmentation + tracking) → distortion correction → Gaussian splatting reconstruction
Before/after comparison: raw frames vs. final 3D render (highlighting specular highlights and corrected lens distortion)
Error/occlusion heatmap or per-region quality chart to show robustness across cluttered backgrounds and rotating wheels
Illustration of Gaussian splats overlayed on corrected camera frustums (iconic depiction of splats vs. mesh)
paper_title: Drive-Through 3D Vehicle Exterior Reconstruction via Dynamic-Scene SfM and Distortion-Aware Gaussian Splatting
paper_authors: Nitin Kulkarni, Akhil Devarashetti, Charlie Cluss, Livio Forte, Philip Schneider
